newsitem.title: BELARUS: Don't let arrest affect ties, Belarus tells Moscow.
newsitem.headline: Don't let arrest affect ties, Belarus tells Moscow.

text.p: Belarus, responding to a protest by Russian President Boris Yeltsin, told Moscow on Wednesday not to make a political issue out of its detention of a Russian television crew.
"Yes, Belarus hears what Russia is saying. But this incident cannot influence important joint policy," Foreign Minister Ivan Antonovich told Reuters.
"The two states have many common problems and Russia has many problems in which it needs Belarussian support."
Yeltsin said earlier on Wednesday the Kremlin might revise a union charter and other accords on closer integration with Belarus if the row was not settled.

Interfax news agency quoted Yeltsin as asking reporters at the Volzhsky Utyos holiday residence in central Russia to convey his words to Belarus hardline President Alexander Lukashenko: "I am indignant over your actions. I want you to explain what is happening."
Belarus arrested the ORT team on Saturday for what Belarus authorities said was illegally filming and crossing the Belarus-Lithuania border.
The ORT correspondent, Pavel Sheremet, had been stripped of his Belarus foreign press accreditation earlier this month.
Yeltsin said he hoped the incident could be settled, but if it was not, it would be time to rethink their ties.
"Let us reconsider the charter and the agreements which we have signed," he said. "We do not touch Belarus journalists."
Antonovich responded: "Their president can say harsh words, but that's it. Relations between our countries should not change just because a former ORT correspondent was detained."

In May Lukashenko signed a charter on a loose union between his country of 10 million and the 150 million-strong Russia. The deal was watered down by liberals in Moscow who feared it would give the hardline president too much say in Russia's policy.
